strategy_pt:
Bats are weak and unless an explorer is unprepared, mainly an annoyance. Their flight patterns are quick and erratic and they quickly attack once before fluttering away, giving only a brief window to strike before they are out of range. Their small size and erratic movements makes shooting them with arrows very challenging and after attacking they often fly behind icicles or indestructible rock features hanging from the ceiling before coming back for another attack run.

While they do not do much damage, they do attack in groups of 4-10 which typically spawn in vertical shafts. An explorer might be attacked while attempting to descend or while they are precariously perched on an edge. Due to some weapons "pulling" the character forward when attacking, a careless player may find themselves taking a quick trip to the bottom of the cave, dying at the hands of the bats' greatest ally: gravity.

Alert explorers will recognize the sounds of the bats and be able to kill them as they approach with a single hit, though often the hitboxes of weapons are in the wrong vertical plane to attack the bats if they attack at a steep angle from above or below. If the player's first attack misses, blocking and waiting for the bats to draw near again may be the best option due to their tendency to fly up and away and hide behind an obstacle on the ceiling, making ranged attacks difficult. It is easiest to fight them with a quick striking weapon such as a sword or knife while you are on flat ground and your back in a corner to minimize their angles of attack. Weapons with a large area of effect attack such asStagbreaker,Iron sledge, or the secondary attack of an atgeir are very effective at clearing out a swarm. Weapons with narrow arcs such as spears or the atgeir's primary attack can make it difficult to connect a strike.

If at all possible, do not try to fight a bat swarm inside or near one of your own structures. Their erratic flight patterns and the somewhat inexact damage dealt by most weapons will have you smashing more of your own stuff than bats. They are best fought in a wide-open area. One method of controlling the "You Stirred the Cauldron" raid is to buildbonfiresorwindmillswithin your base. Then, stand near the bonfire or windmill. When the bats attack you, they will either dive into the fire or the rotating blades of the windmill and die. You'll have to repair the bonfire or windmill during and after the raid if you use this strategy. If you have a covered pen for tamed animals, make sure that all openings are either very narrow or are covered with iron gratings.

strategy_pt:
Cultists are very alert to their surroundings and will move to sources of noise making sneaking up on them difficult if the player is breaking objects or fighting creatures nearby. Despite this, they will not open the doors that separate their worked stone lairs from the natural caves.

Their opening attack is a burst of flame that explodes before them. This attack will do initial fire damage and leave players burning for 5 seconds.  This attack cannot be blocked or parried and encompasses a wide arc. After using this attack they will attack twice with a flaming claw slash that will also leave the player burning for 5 seconds in addition to the physical damage. They will cycle through between the attacks with the same flame/claw/claw cycle as long as they are alive or lose track of the player which resets their cycle.

Dodging, rolling to the side, or backpedaling can get the player out of the way of the flame burst since it is a relatively short-range attack. It is also blocked by solid objects such as a wall or door.

Their claw attacks can be blocked or parried but likeFenrings, they are only staggered for a very brief period of time.

If a player has access toFire resistance barley winethen the Cultist's flame attacks and burning affect from their claws are very minor, though the claws still do physical damage. They are very susceptible tospirit damageandpoison damage. So silver weapons, includingFrostner, are very effective.poison,silver, orneedlearrows are also effective. Silver arrows are the most effective, but the resources may be probably better spent crafting or upgrading aDraugr Fangto use with a different arrow type, preferably poison, sincepoison arrowsstack with the poison effect of the Draugr Fang.

strategy_pt:
Directly attacking a Dvergr settlement will result in the Dvergr in that immediate area becoming permanently hostile to the player. Over time, however, most Dvergr settlements will be overrun by attacking Seekers, especially where the settlement does not have any Dvergr mages. Gjall and seeker soldiers can be particularly useful if you can draw them in to assist you and do some or all of your work for you. At the very least, it's worth letting them soften up the Dvergr before attacking them yourself.

Because dvergr are naturally neutral to the player, the player can choose when and how to attack them.

If your Viking is trying to get resources from a Dvergr structure such asdvergr extractorsorsoft tissuefrom crates, without aggroing the dwarves,refined eitror evenpufferfishmay be tossed to land next to a dwarf and will gradually kill it without aggroing the Dvergr. You can also avoid killing the Dvergr at all by tossing refined eitr, one by one, right next to award, extractor box, or crate. The radiation from the refined eitr will eventually break the ward or box.

The Hard Way:

If you are attacking groups of Dvergr or Dvergr settlements directly without assistance from seekers, gjall, or indirect damage sources (pufferfish, refined eitr, etc.), planning is extremely important. 1 and especially 2-star mages are some of your largest threats and should most likely be taken out first. 2-star rogues also hit particularly hard and should never be underestimated. Staggering and killing one of the strongest Dvergr should be one of your strongest considerations when starting a fight, and preferably when they are separated from other Dvergr. They can bepushedby nudging them around as you walk into them, but keep in mind that they may decide to path right back to the spot that you pushed them away from and regroup.

High ground can be extremely useful, especially if the route to your spot is difficult for Dvergr to navigate towards. To this end, ranged attacks (both physical and magical) can be a way to bypass some of the difficulty if the distance to your spot is far and your aim is precise.

Ultimately, groups of players are your best bet for taking on groups of Dvergr. For solo players, aiming for summoned help from aDead Raiserwould be ideal if you can contend with the heavy Eitr requirement. These fights are often less predictable that you might expect, and any help you can get should be utilized. Even multiplayer groups should consider having at least one player using a dead raiser (paired with aStaff of Protectionto bubble playersandtheSkelettminions) for the additional help.

strategy_pt:
Individual Ticks are easily dealt with. They are vulnerable to pierce damage and thus weapons dealing particular damage type such as thePorcupinewill reliably kill multiple Ticks in a single hit. If a Tick attaches itself to the player, it will begin to deal heavy pierce damage over time. Attached ticks can be reliably removed by using a combat roll. The default keybind: block (RMB) + jump (spacebar) keys. Alternatively, the player can attempt to use area-of-effect damage to kill the attached Tick (any sledge  hammer type weapon works well), or (with the right angle and timing) parrying the Tick's attack. TheRoot armor'spierce resistance provides great protection against Tick attacks.

A shield can block or parry ticks, allowing them to be disposed of quickly. Because ticks move very quickly and jump frequently when pursuing a target, ranged attacks are usually ineffective once they have spotted a player; however, idle ticks move very slowly and infrequently, and thus ranged attacks are highly effective against them in this state (usually at a distance to keep from being noticed by them). In either case,0-starticks have relatively low health - much more than aDeathsquito, but still low enough that they usually die in one hit from almost anyPlains-tier weapon or better.

1-star and 2-star ticks have increased health and may require multiple hits to kill, unlike the common tick. 2-star ticks especially are capable of killing unprepared players in under one second; players wearing light armor (such as theEitr-weave Set) are especially vulnerable to them.

Since ticks are often encountered in groups, area-of-effect attacks are highly useful for eliminating them simultaneously. Some area-of-effect weapons (such as atgeirs, e.g. theBlack metal atgeir) are less useful due to being less able to hit targets at different altitudes, thus likely missing jumping ticks and being generally less useful in the uneven terrain found throughout the Mistlands. Other weapons (such as two-handed clubs like theDemolisheror magic weapons like theStaff of Embers) work well in all terrain; the staff of embers in particular is highly useful due to being a ranged area-of-effect attack, capable of defeating multiple ticks at once from afar.

If they latch onto a player, some options include:

Use an area-effect weapon, such as the atgeir or two-handed club, to damage and knockback ticks.A roll will remove ticks attached to the player.Swinging a weapon while turning around allows the weapon to hit ticks on the character's back.Using anOoze bomborBile bomb, their persisting AoE can kill ticks easily.The damage from an attached tick can still be blocked as if they were attacks, and a successful parry will result in the tick being detached.

strategy_pt:
Charred Warriors have a somewhat slow walking animation, meaning they can be outran easily.

Warriors have different attack animations, such as a forward thrust or a delayed swing. These make parrying less predictable before their animations are learned.

Most attacks are equally effective on warriors (except for non-backstab/ambush pierce attacks), so your best approach is being patient with the fight and with your stamina and/or eitr.

Ranged players should keep in mind that warriors can occasionally be fairly quiet and have the tendency to sneak up on players that are busy focusing on other enemies or trying to catch their breath. If the player is wearing lighter armor or heavily relying on a bubble from aStaff of Protection, multiple warriors thrusting at the same exact time are likely to execute you quickly if they catch you in a blind spot.

The same can occur even for those that prefer heavier armor and/or the use of shields, as multiple thrusts from warriors within a short window can overwhelm your stagger limitations. Even players that prefer health-centered diets will find that food doesn't help if multiple warriors are striking at the same exact moment.

Try to separate them if you can, rely on teammates, split them up and/or distract them with minion summons from aDead Raiser/Trollstav. Additionally, it's worth noting that fleeing/retreating into other nearby areas with more enemies (notably warriors) can lead to a false sense of security with their slower walking speed. The number of warriors can quickly turn the favor of the fight against you, and planning your routes out can help prevent 1 minute fights from turning into 10 minute brawls.

strategy_pt:
Charred Marksmen have two attacks, a burst shot when the player is farther away, and a single direct shot when the player is closer. The direct shot can be parried, akin to a Draugr with a bow.

They are best dealt with by attacking them in melee range, rather than with a ranged weapon, due to their resistance toPierce. However, ranged exceptions include heavy backstab/ambush damage from either anArbalestorRipper(especially aWound Ripperif used in tandem with blood magic), as well as Eitr options like theStaff of the Wild,Staff of Embers, or theStaff of Fracturing.

Staff of the wild can give an Eitr caster the option to wear down marksmen, as most assume a stationary position when in range and within an unblocked view of the player.The Staff of Embers can deal fairly consistent damage without needing to be extremely accurate with hits- as the area of effect damage can still burn down targets.The Staff of Fracturing can also be reliable, but only when landing direct hits that allow the full cluster of fractured shots to detonate on the marksman. Missed projectiles are likely to only set the marksman on fire, which will have negligible results.

Lastly, minions should typically be reserved for larger clusters of diversified enemies, but they still remain an option for marksmen that aren't being dealt with by the methods above.SkelettandSummoned trollminions from theDead RaiserandTrollstavcan help distract and mitigate incoming damage from groups of marksmen if utilized properly at the cost of requiring heavy Eitr management.  Though in the case of the Trollstav, it is best to be ready to kill leftover, aggressive minions that have survived the fight.

strategy_pt:
Voltures will attempt to get behind the player and attack with their talons. If the player turns toward the Volture to attack it, it will attempt to fly up in the air can get behind the player again. Additionally, Voltures are among the fastest enemies in the game and can outrun a player in light armor with the full effect ofWind Run, making them especially dangerous to players with very low health.

Voltures deal little damage and do not have very much health, but their speed and tendency to get behind the player can make them a nuisance (and a threat in larger numbers). Care should be taken when fighting other enemies when nearby Voltures, since the latter can potentially get behind the player and block them in.

Voltures can only be encountered in two locations in theAshlandsbiome: aroundVolture nests(where several may spawn, butonly one time: they willnotrespawn there periodically), or randomly in areas at or below sea level. Besides one-time encounters around nests, this does mean that Voltures are encountered chiefly at the coastline of the Ashlands, where they can spawn slightly offshore; they are much more rarely encountered inland as random spawns, since low altitudes are rare there (sometimes,lavasections can have low enough altitudes that Voltures can spawn there, although they are not immune to lava and will quickly die if they touch it). Voltures often spawn just far enough out to sea that they are not highly likely to spot players who remain on dry land; however, wading out into the waters towards them (but remaining in water shallow enough to stand in) is usually sufficient to attract their attention.

Area of effect attacks are effective when dealing with Voltures, for similar reasons to how they work well againstBats- their rapid movement and tendency to approach from awkward angles makes AoE damage an easier way of dealing with them, especially in numbers; their low health means they die quickly even to relatively-inferior weaponry (e.g. even aBlack metal atgeir's secondary attack is still capable of two-shotting Voltures). Good weapon options for dealing with Voltures which are Ashlands-appropriate include theHimminafl(secondary attack), theDemolisher, and theStaff of Embers(for mages); especially the latter two, due to their spherical hit areas (polearms' secondary attacks hit in a flat circle, which can more easily miss Voltures if they are not very near your own altitude).

With appropriate weapons, players should have little to fear from Voltureson their own, even with onlyMistlands-tier armor, since they can be dealt with quickly before they can start piling up damage. Voltures are more dangerous when they join battle with other creatures - as is often the case in the Ashlands, due to its high spawn rates. Voltures are high-priority targets in these situations: they must be dealt with rapidly or they will begin stacking damage on players, as well as interfering with their ability to combat the other creatures and placing them at risk on those fronts.

Other options include theArbalestandRippervariants for backstab/ambush damage, especially when traveling in groups via theDrakkar. Having a crossbowman (or archer) on board with decent aim will save you the trouble of dealing with close range fights that might result in damaging your own ship. On land, ensure that you're looking for spots that you can keep your back to and swivel around if need be so that you can better deal with incoming swipes at your blind spots.
